limitations: Reviewed complete landfarming helper per one kg of wet sewage sludge containing 97% water, generated by wastewater treatment of leachate from sanitary landfilling of waste packaging paper. The source reference is -1 kg and the helper reference is +1 kg: apply factor -1 to caller demand while preserving actual signed credits. Retain all 39 reported biosphere quantities, including fossil and biogenic CO2, ammonia, N2O, nitrate, phosphate, soil metals, soil waste heat, and separate air and groundwater water volumes. Canonical ecoinvent biospheres retain the exact published source flow definitions, signed quantities and units. This helper authorizes no ionic-metal or receiving-compartment proxy. Only the marked non-hazardous-waste inventory indicator may be omitted where unsupported, with a warning under the standing policy; no physical release may be dropped. Keep exactly 0.00097087 m3 of vacuum-tanker service per kg wet sludge. Do not derive a density adjustment, multiply by 97%, normalize to dry solids or add transport. The inspected complete Swiss service includes pumping, spreading, fuel, tractor, tanker and shed; it explicitly excludes sludge production and sludge releases. The Swiss UVEK service replaces the source global CH, US, CA-QC and RoW mixture without a fuel-consumption or tank-capacity adjustment. Native and ecoinvent Swiss suppliers both use 0.217 kg diesel, 0.0563 kg tanker, 0.0275 kg tractor and 0.00019 m2 shed per m3. The native background reports 1.08e-8 kg chromium VI to air and 9.84 MJ waste heat to air; the inspected Swiss ecoinvent supplier reports chromium III at that mass and no waste-heat record. These are disclosed whole-background-supplier differences, not permission to relabel the sludge's direct chromium-III release. LCIA scores, engine emissions, vintage, field conditions and regional backgrounds can differ. Add no fertilizer production, avoided fertilizer, manure supply, collection freight, landfill or extra wastewater-treatment burden. Preserve caller uncertainty, formulas, metadata, foreground suppliers, production and separately listed emissions. Internal source formulas and uncertainty are not reconstructed. Include all returned helpers in scoring and export. The existing native-to-ecoinvent Swiss spreading correspondence was inspected independently and remains unchanged. Only the four enumerated exact cut-off profiles are approved. Native UVEK 2026 soil-ion and groundwater-volume correspondences require independent biosphere review; missing physical correspondences reject and roll back conversion under the default coverage policy rather than silently changing or omitting releases. Canonical ecoinvent-biosphere UVEK 2025/2026 conversions retain all emissions. This technosphere approval does not imply complete native-biosphere coverage. No patch, model, version or inverse waste-treatment fallback is inferred.
